topics.title: Packaging of Processed Food | Reasons for Packaging of Processed Food Primary 6/Basic 6 Term 2 Week 2 Agriculture
topics.content:
AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 2
PRIMARY 6
THEME -
PREVIOUS LESSON - As Stated in Second Term (Term 2) Week 1 Plan Lesson Notes for Primary Schools
TOPIC - PACKAGING OF PROCESSED FOOD
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Packaging of Processed Food
3. Reasons for Packaging of Processed Food
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. identified packaged food.
2. justify reasons for packaging of processed food.
3. devise means to package produce harvest from school farm.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identified processed food.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of sample of package food or chart showing processed food.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
PACKAGING
Packaging are materials used for wrapping or protecting goods for distribution, storage, sale or personal use.
PACKAGING MATERIALS
1. Cup
2. Can
2. Plastic
3. Bottle
4. Polythene
5. Paper and paperboard
6. Drum/barrels
7. Cages
8. Boxes
9. Aluminium foil
10. Trays, etc.
PROCESSED FOOD
Processed food is the transformation of agricultural products into food and beverages.
For example,
Fish - Titus
Meat - corned beef
Cocoa - milo or bourvita
Fruit - juice
ASSIGNMENT
Find out,
1. the meaning of packaging of processed food.
2. 5 food package containers.
3. the reasons for packaging of processed food.
LESSON 2 - PACKAGING OF PROCESSED FOOD
Packaging of processed food is the process of enclosing or protecting processed foods for personal or commercial use.
EXAMPLES OF PACKAGING OF PROCESSED FOOD
1. Titus
2. Milo or bourvita
3. Popcorn
4. Yogurt
5. Gala, etc.
REASONS FOR PACKAGING OF PROCESSED FOOD
The following are the reasons for packaging of processed food,
1. Personal or commercial use
2. To prevent the food from contamination.
3. To prevent physical damage.
4. To increase sales.
5. To retain the original shape and texture.
6. To maintain freshness of the food.
7. To increase shelf life of the food.
8. To prevent waste.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps - he/she,
1. Revises the previous lesson based on the pupil’s related knowledge or experience.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in lesson review.
2. Displays samples of empty food packages.
3. Asks pupils to state the products of the package.
4. Guides pupils to identify and state the source of the products.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and state the source of the products.
5. Uses the activity 2 - 4 and pupil’s responses to introduce the lesson.
6. Leads a discussion on the meaning of packaging processed food with appropriate examples.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the discussing the meaning of packaging processed food.
7. Displays samples of package professed food.
8. Uses the assignment and samples of package professed food to lead pupils to discuss the meaning of packaging professed food.
Pupil’s Activities - Use their finding to define packaging professed food.
9. Guides pupils to analyze the package professed food and state the reasons for packaging processed food.
Pupil’s Activities - Analyze the package professed food and state the reasons for packaging processed food.
10. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in lesson summary and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Types of Packaging - Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Packaging Primary 6/Basic 6 Term 2 Week 3 Agriculture
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. explain the meaning packaged food and processed food.
2. give 5 food that can be processed with appropriate examples.
4. state 5 reasons for packaging of processed food.
3. devise means to process and package maize.

topics.content:
AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 3
PRIMARY 6
THEME -  PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Packaging of Processed Food | Reasons for Packaging of Processed Food Primary 6/Basic 6 Term 2 Week 2 Agriculture
TOPIC - TYPES OF PACKAGING
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Types of Packaging
3. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. identify the types of packaging.
2. give examples of each type of packaging.
3. produce their own packaged products.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify packaged products.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of sample of packaged products or chart showing packaged products.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
PACKAGING
Packaging are materials used for wrapping or protecting goods for distribution, storage, sale or personal use.
Cup, can, plastic, bottle, polythene, paper or paperboard, etc. are materials used for packaging products.
TYPES OF PACKAGING
There are three (3) types of packaging,
1. Primary packaging
2. Secondary packaging
3. Tertiary packaging
ASSIGNMENT
Find the meaning of primary, secondary and tertiary packaging with appropriate examples.
LESSON 2 - TYPES OF PACKAGING
PRIMARY PACKAGING
Primary packaging is the package that has direct contact with the products.
It is used used to protect or preserve the product from contamination.
Primary packaging is known as unit or consumer packaging because it is what the consumer sees at sale point.
This kind of packaging is designed for the consumers.
Examples of primary,
- One pack of indomine
- One tin of peak milk
- One pack of mini cracker
- One pack maggi cube
- One bottle coke, etc.
SECONDARY PACKAGING
Secondary packaging is the packaging of two or more primary packages.
This kind of packaging is designed for the middlemen.
Examples of secondary packaging are,
- One carton of indomine - 40 packs
- One carton of peak milk - 24 tins
- One carton of mini cracker - 150 packs
- One satchel of Knorr chicken - 50 cubes
- One create of coke - 24 bottles
TERTIARY PACKAGING
Tertiary packaging is the packaging of two or more secondary packages.
It is used to package larger quantities or protect shipping products.
Tertiary packaging is known as bulk or transit packaging.
This kind of packaging is designed mainly for the wholesalers.
Examples of tertiary packaging are,
- brown cardboard boxes
- wood pallets
- shrink wrap
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps - he/she,
1. Revises the previous lesson based on the pupil’s related knowledge or experience.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in lesson review.
2. Displays one of three or five processed food. For examples - indomine, tin milk, coaster biscuit, knorr chicken and bottle of coke.
3. Asks pupils to identify and state the number of each product in carton if indomine, tin milk and coater biscuit, satchel of Knorr chicken and create of coke.
Pupil’s Activities - Response to the questions correctly.
4. Uses pupils responses to introduce the lesson - types of packaging.
5. Explains and illustrates each types of packaging.
Pupil’s Activities - Pay attention to the lesson introduction to understand the concept of each type of packaging.
6. Asks pupils to find the meaning of each type of packaging.
Pupil’s Activities - find the meaning of each type of packaging at home.
7. Uses pupil’s findings to lead a discussion on the types of packaging with appropriate examples.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the class discussion.
8. Guides pupils to identify the similarities and differences between each type of packaging with appropriate examples.
Pupils Activities - State produce their own packaged products.
9. Guides pupils in pairs or groups to produce their own packaged products.
Pupil’s Activities - Produce their own packaged products.
10. Asks pupils to analyze the importance of packaged products.
Pupil’s Activities - State the importance of packaging.
11. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in lesson summary and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Materials Used for Packaging | Importance of Packaging Primary 6/Basic 6 Term 2 Week 4 Agriculture
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. state 3 types of packaging.
2. give 5 examples of each type of packaging.
3. discuss the relationship and the different between each type of packaging.
5. produce their own packaged products.

AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 4
PRIMARY 6
THEME - PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Types of Packaging - Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Packaging Primary 6/Basic 6 Term 2 Week 3 Agriculture
TOPIC - PACKAGING MATERIALS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Materials Used for Packaging
3. Importance of Packaging
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. identify packaged materials.
2. justify the importance of packaged goods.
3. assemble materials used for packaging processed goods.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify materials appropriate for different processed goods.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of sample of package food or chart showing processed food.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
PACKAGING
Packaging are materials used for wrapping or protecting goods for distribution, storage, sale or personal use.
PACKAGING MATERIALS
Materials used for packaging processed goods are,
1. Cup
2. Can
2. Plastic
3. Bottle
4. Polythene
5. Paper and paperboard
6. Drum/barrels
7. Cages
8. Boxes
9. Aluminium foil
10. Trays, etc.
LESSON 2 - IMPORTANCE OF PACKAGING
The importance of packaging goods are -
1. It protects the goods.
2. It promotes the goods.
3. It attracts consumers.
4. It differentiates goods from one another.
5. It increases sales.
6. It provides information about the goods. For examples - manufacture date, expiry date, etc.
7. it enhances usability.
8. It increases shelf life of the food.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps - he/she,
1. Revises the previous lesson based on the pupil’s related knowledge or experience.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in lesson review.
2. Displays samples of goods with different packaging or chart showing different materials used for packaging goods.
3. Lets pupils identify, examine and different the packaging materials.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and state each of the materials used for packaging each goods.
4. Guides pupils to analyze and justify the importance of packaging.
Pupil’s Activities - Analyze and justify the importance of packaging.
6. Organizes a trip to the nearest supermarket where there are different packaged processed goods.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the excursion to identify different materials used for packaging processed food to justify the importance of packaging as discussed in the lesson.
7. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in lesson summary and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Reasons for Packaging Farm Produce | Materials Used for Packaging Farm Produce Primary 6/Basic 6 Term 2 Week 5 Agriculture
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. state 5 packaged materials.
2. justify the importance of packaged goods.
3. assemble materials used for packaging processed goods.

topics.title: Reasons for Packaging Farm Produce | Materials Used for Packaging Farm Produce Primary 6/Basic 6 Term 2 Week 5 Agriculture
topics.content:
AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 5
PRIMARY 6
THEME - PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Materials Used for Packaging | Importance of Packaging Primary 6/Basic 6 Term 2 Week 4 Agriculture
TOPIC - PACKAGING MATERIALS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Materials Used for Packaging Farm Produce
3. Reasons for Packaging Farm Produce
3. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. identify materials used for packaging farm produce.
2. give reasons why farm produce are packaged.
3. justify reasons for using some materials for a particular farm produce, for examples - create for eggs, cage for life animals, basket for tomatoes, etc.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify farm produce.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of sample of farm produce or chart showing farm produce.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Farm produce is the crop and other agricultural product produced and sold by farmers.
Examples of farm produce are,
- Crops - yam, beans, potatoes, maize, etc.
- Animals - poultry, eggs, goat, cow, etc.
- Other agricultural products - honey, seeds, fresh cut flowers, etc.
Farm produce can be processed and packaged or packaged directly depending on the nature of the products.
PACKAGING FARM PRODUCE
Packaging farm produce is the wrapping of farm produce with suitable materials to protect for easy distribution, storage, sale or personal use.
PACKAGING MATERIALS
Materials used for packaging farm produce are,
1. Baskets
2. Cages - live animals
3. Trays or creates
4. Sacks or bags
5. Boxes
6. Polythene bags
7. Plastic containers
Note - Guides pupils to analyze and justify the reasons for using the above for a particular product. For examples - create for eggs not basket, basket for tomatoes not sack, etc.
LESSON 2 - REASONS FOR PACKAGING FARM PRODUCE
1. Personal or commercial use.
2. To prevent the food from contamination.
3. To prevent physical damage.
4. To increase sales.
5. To retain the original shape and texture.
6. To maintain freshness of the food.
7. To increase shelf life of the food.
8. To prevent waste.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps - he/she,
1. Revises the previous lesson based on the pupil’s related knowledge or experience.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in lesson review.
2. Displays samples or chart of farm produce.
3. Asks pupils to identify and group as crops and animals farm produce.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and group the samples or contents of the chart as crops or animals.
4. Displays samples or chart of different packaging items for farm produce.
3. Lets pupils identify and describe the use of the packaging items for farm produce.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and describe the use of the packaging items for farm produce.
4. Uses the samples or chart and pupil’s responses to introduce the lesson - packaging farm produce.
Pupil’s Activities - Pay attention to lesson introduction to understand the concept of packaging farm produce.
5. Leads a discussion on the meaning of farm produce with appropriate examples and the materials used for packaging them.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the lesson discussion.
7. Displays chart showing packaging items for different farm produce.
8. Asks pupils to state the reasons why packaging item best for the farm produce.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify different packaging items used for farm produce and state the reasons why packaging items are best for them.
9. Asks pupils to mention packaging item that’s best for crops and animals or specific crops and animals.
Pupil’s Activities - Mention packaging items used for crops and animals with appropriate examples.
10. Asks pupils in groups or pairs to list packaging materials, analyze and justify the reasons for each materials.
Pupil’s Activities - State the materials used for packaging materials and reasons for using them.
11. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in lesson summary and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. explain the meaning of farm produce.
2. state 5 materials used for packaging farm produce with appropriate examples.
3. describe each of packaging material mentioned in question 2.
4. give reasons why farm produce are packaged.
5. justify the reasons for using the packaging materials stated in question 2.
6. justify the reasons for using create for eggs, cage for life animals, basket for tomatoes, etc.
